correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact held-input ODE in the two-dimensional safety-trigger counterexample, with J skew-symmetric, x(t_i+tau)=e^{h_i tau/2}R(tau)x_i, h(t_i+tau)=1-(1-h_i)e^{h_i tau}, and E_i(tau)^2=(1-h_i)[(e^{h_i tau/2}-1)^2+4e^{h_i tau/2}sin^2(tau/2)]. For rho>1, 0<sigma<1, and nonzero strictly interior x_0 (0<h_0<1), the residual changes sign before the first barrier-zero time, giving a positive trigger. The barriers decrease; if they had a positive limiting value, the bounded speed and trigger magnitude would imply a positive lower bound on each inter-event duration and each barrier decrement, contradiction. Hence h_i->0. The exact error at any fixed small delta>0 tends to 2 sin(delta/2)>0, showing first trigger tau_i->0; the local flow then gives E_i(tau_i)/tau_i->1. With c=sigma/(2rho^3), tau_i/h_{i+1}->c and h_{i+1}/h_i->1; the reciprocal increment 1/h_{i+1}-1/h_i->c. Stolz-Cesàro yields h_i~1/(ci), tau_i~1/i, and summing gives t_i~log i, log N(t)/t->1. The latter is a logarithmic event-count asymptotic, not the stronger N(t)~e^t. The divergent harmonic sum excludes finite-time Zeno accumulation. Independently calculated 20,000 exact held-flow roots, verifying positive decreasing h and i*tau_i tending near 1; finite checks corroborate but are not the asymptotic proof.

value.rationale: This sharp asymptotic resolves an important distinction in a canonical safety-control counterexample: infimum of inter-event gaps equals zero while events do not accumulate in finite time. The universal leading gap constant and exact barrier coefficient quantify the sampling burden, and t_i~log i distinguishes infinite-time exponential growth of counts from Zeno behavior. It is specifically motivated by the earlier counterexample and is not asserted as a general controller theorem.
